sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: L3/L4: all Halo- and SNAP-tagged receptors including ALK4 positively detected by impermeable CA-Alexa488 / BG-Alexa488 staining, confirming cell-surface display. L1/L2: HA-ALK4 showed typical FRAP curves confirming surface display and lateral diffusion. Signaling function of the tagged receptor was NOT MEASURED in either study.
sites.rationale: L3 explicitly places the tag 'downstream the signal peptide sequence,' which by the authoritative landmarks means after residue 23 (last SP residue, G) and before residue 24 (mature N-terminus, S). Python confirms seq[22]='G' and seq[23]='S'. The junction is 103 residues from the TM boundary (127), well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. L1/L2 independently confirm a full-length membrane-anchored HA/myc-tagged ALK4 with the tag on the extracellular domain; since the C-terminus is intracellular, topology derivation yields the identical junction, providing strong corroboration. L3/L4 (PMC9837045): full-length ALK4/ACVR1B N-terminally fused with Halo- or SNAP-tags via a 5x glycine linker placed explicitly downstream of the signal peptide sequence, expressed in mammalian cells as part of a BMP/TGFβ receptor library. L1/L2 (PMC8855587) independently corroborate the same junction: full-length HA-ALK4 or myc-ALK4 expressed in COS7 cells with the tag on the extracellular domain, confirmed by surface FRAP.

sources.claim: BMP/TGFβ receptors, including type I receptors (hALK1-ALK6, rALK7, and hALK2-R206H) and type II receptors (hACVR2A, hACVR2B, hBMPR2, and hTGFBR2) were, therefore, N-terminally fused with Halo- or SNAP-tags separated by a 5x glycine linker downstream the signal peptide sequence, to obtain the receptor library shown in Fig. 1c .

literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) converge on a single junction: the N-terminal extracellular position immediately after signal-peptide cleavage (after residue 23). L3/L4 pin it explicitly ('downstream the signal peptide sequence'); L1/L2 name no residue but the protein has only one extracellular terminus (C-terminus is intracellular), so topology derivation yields the same site. Because both papers target the same junction, this is reported as one site grounded in L3 (the more explicit evidence), with L1/L2 as corroboration. No internal extracellular loop insertions are reported in the ledger for ACVR1B. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are named in the ledger.
